extracted.intended_audience: depositors of biological material for patent purposes (biotech patent applicants and their patent agents) and culture collection administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Detailed procedural, technical and administrative requirements that UK culture collections (IMI, CCAP, ECACC, NCTC, NCYC, NCIMB, etc.) impose for making, converting and furnishing Budapest Treaty patent deposits of microorganisms, cell lines, plasmids, seeds and related material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kinds of Microorganisms that May Be Deposited
rubrics_metrics.description: Specification of which taxa/kinds of material each collection accepts (e.g., freshwater and terrestrial algae and free living protozoa for CCAP; animal and human cell lines, genetically modified cell lines, hybridomas, viruses, eukaryotic and viral recombinant DNA for ECACC; bacteria preserved by freeze-drying and pathogenic to man/animals for NCTC; yeasts not known pathogens for NCYC; bacteria, yeasts and bacteriophages up to ACDP Group 2 for NCIMB).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collections list allowable categories and reserve the right to refuse material they deem technically unsuitable or unsafe. Some collections accept specific forms of material only (e.g., frozen ampoules, lyophilized cultures). Hazardous materials may require additional approvals (e.g., ECACC requires a biohazard risk assessment and HSE authorization for certain GMOs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and Quantity of Deposit
rubrics_metrics.description: Required physical form and minimum number of replicates/ampoules/cell counts for deposit (examples: CCAP: liquid or agar slope cultures, minimum six replicates; CCAP algal cultures 10^2 to 10^4 cell/ml or three plants for seaweeds; ECACC animal cell cultures: frozen cultures, minimum 12 replicates, at least 4 x 10^6 cells/ampoule; ECACC plasmids/phage: minimum 12 ampoules; NCTC: one culture accepted lyophilized or in agar slabs; NCYC: two replicates for lyophilized and two for agar slope; NCIMB: must withstand freeze-drying or liquid nitrogen).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositors must supply material in the required format and quantity; insufficient packaging (e.g., not enough dry ice) can cause refusal. Some materials (e.g., naked DNA) have recommended buffers. Requirements vary by collection and organism type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum Viability/Concentration Specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerical minimum viability or concentration specifications when stated (e.g., CCAP algal cultures 10^2 to 10^4 cell/ml depending on species; ECACC animal cells >=4 x 10^6 cells/ampoule; NCYC/other collections give analogous minimums or require culturability).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositors should ensure cultures meet stated minimum counts or culturability; where species-specific variation exists, follow collection guidance or negotiate (e.g., protozoa counts decided by negotiation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time Required for Viability Testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Average and possible maximum durations for viability testing prior to acceptance (examples: CCAP average 7 days, may take up to 35 days; ECACC viruses 21–28 days, animal cell cultures 14–21 days, recombinant DNA 14 days; NCTC average 4 days, may take up to 14 days; NCYC average 5 days, up to 14 days).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositors should allow for stated average times and be prepared for longer tests in some cases; customers will be advised if testing may take longer (ECACC).

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositor Checks and Renewal of Stocks
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies on whether the collection prepares its own batches, how stocks are renewed, and what authenticity checks the depositor must perform (e.g., many collections prepare their own batches by subculturing and require the depositor to test authenticity samples of the first batch; some store original material only temporarily or not at all unless cryopreserved).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositors should be prepared to provide replacement material if stocks diminish, and to perform authenticity checks on the first batch. Collections differ on whether they keep original material (cryopreserved exceptions noted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Language of Communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Official language used by the collection for communications (e.g., English is the official language for CCAP, ECACC, NCTC, NCYC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications in other languages are not accepted; depositors must supply forms and information in the collection's official language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract Terms on Application Form
rubrics_metrics.description: The application form constitutes a contract binding the depositor to terms such as providing necessary information, replacing material if collection cannot furnish samples, paying fees, indemnifying the collection (except for collection negligence), not withdrawing deposit during required storage period, and authorizing furnishing of samples per patent requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositors should read and accept contractual obligations; some collections require a supplement stating whether the depositor acts personally or on behalf of an organization (NCTC).

rubrics_metrics.name: Import and Quarantine Regulations / Biohazard Statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Deposits may be subject to import/quarantine rules and biohazard regulatory documentation (e.g., ECACC requires a biohazard risk assessment before sending deposits; NCTC notes importation rules for animal pathogens; NCIMB acceptance of seeds subject to Plant Health (Great Britain) Order 1987).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositors must ensure regulatory paperwork is in place; high-containment processing may take longer and cost more. Some collections will advise on required documentation or ask depositors to obtain it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making the Original Deposit — Required Forms and Notifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Collections require specific accession/deposit forms (model BP/2, collection-specific accession forms, deposit and biohazard statements) and issue official receipts and viability statements on mandatory international forms (BP/4, BP/5, BP/9) or collection versions (e.g., CC PF3, CC PF5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositors must complete the required forms (collection-specific plus treaty forms) and may receive unofficial advance notification (telephone/fax) of accession number and test results if requested; official documents are issued on international or collection forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion of Previous Deposits
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies on converting deposits made outside the Budapest Treaty into Budapest Treaty deposits (varies by collection: some permit conversion if a new sample is supplied and batches' authenticity checked; others do not permit conversion of non-patent deposits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Converted deposits may be subject to standard storage fees regardless of prior payments; administrative requirements for conversion are generally similar to original deposits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making a New Deposit Procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure for making a new deposit (e.g., completion of BP/2, collection deposit forms, sending copies of required documents per Rule 6.2, notification prior to dispatch, shipping details such as flight number and waybill for air freight in ECACC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositors must follow shipping/notification protocols (e.g., inform ECACC at least 48 hours before dispatch) and supply supporting documentation; failure to follow shipping instructions can lead to refusal or delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official and Unofficial Notifications Practice
rubrics_metrics.description: How and when collections notify depositors: official notifications via mandatory forms; some collections will, if requested, telephone or telex deposit date, accession number and viability test results prior to official form issuance; others do not provide unofficial advance notifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositors can request unofficial communications in some collections but should rely on official documents for legal purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supply of Information to a Patent Agent
rubrics_metrics.description: Collections' policies on supplying receipts and viability statements to a depositor's patent agent (practices vary: some routinely ask for patent agent details and will supply copies to both depositor and agent; others do not routinely ask but will provide copies on request; NCYC supplies to either depositor or agent but not both).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositors should indicate agent details at deposit if they want direct correspondence to their agent and clarify collection-specific practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for Samples — Procedures and Proof of Entitlement
rubrics_metrics.description: Collections' practices for advising third parties on how to request samples, and whether they supply request forms; some provide model BP/12 or office forms where available, others require requestors to obtain forms from industrial property offices. Collections assume requesting parties meet import and handling requirements unless specific checks are needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For requests requiring proof of entitlement, requestors may need to obtain forms from the relevant patent office. Collections may withhold hazardous organisms until appropriate permits/containment proof is provided (e.g., ECACC, IMI, NCTC requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on Furnishing Hazardous Organisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Limitations and prerequisites before furnishing samples of potentially hazardous organisms: IMI and ECACC will furnish plant pathogens only to UK parties with permits; ECACC withholds potentially hazardous organisms until confirmed that requester has appropriate containment facilities; NCTC requires departmental authorization for Hazard Group 3 organisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requestors must provide permits, containment evidence, or departmental authorization as required. For U.S. requests for plant pathogens, IMI sends samples via USDA quarantine authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source of Supplied Samples
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy that samples furnished are usually from the collection's own preparations/batches, often prepared directly from depositor-supplied material without subculture where possible; exceptions include when original material was cryopreserved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collections typically prepare their own batches for distribution; depositors should be aware that samples come from the collection's preparations and may be asked to replace material if stocks are depleted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of the Depositor When Samples Furnished
rubrics_metrics.description: Collections notify depositors by letter when samples of their microorganism have been furnished to third parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositors will receive notification but collections may differ on timing and format of notifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cataloguing of Budapest Treaty Deposits
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether collections list Budapest Treaty deposits in their public catalog (several UK collections state they do not list Budapest Treaty deposits in published catalogs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositors should not expect public catalog listing for treaty deposits unless explicitly stated by the collection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule of Fees — Typical Fee Items
rubrics_metrics.description: Fee categories typically charged: storage of each strain, issuance of a viability statement, furnishing of a sample, issuance of an attestation, communication of information, charges for deposit and storage including certification and viability statement, administration fees, HSE registration charges for GMOs, special containment processing fees, expedition/carriage costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees are collection- and item-specific (examples: IMI storage GBP 600, viability statement GBP 80, sample GBP 55; CCAP storage GBP 600, viability statement GBP 50, furnishing sample GBP 40; ECACC cell line deposit GBP 950 etc.). VAT may apply. High-containment processing and regulatory authorizations incur extra charges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hazard Group / GMO Assessment and Additional Charges
rubrics_metrics.description: Collections require hazard classification (e.g., ACDP Group, ACGM activity class) and may charge extra or require authorization for GMOs or Level 4 organisms (ECACC: ACGM 2–4 assessment and HSE registration charge; NCIMB: Class 2 GMOs accepted case-by-case with longer processing and extra administrative expenses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositors of GMOs or high-hazard materials must allow additional time and budget for regulatory approval processes and associated fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositor Obligations Regarding Replacement and Non-withdrawal
rubrics_metrics.description: Depositor obligations commonly include replacing material at their expense if the collection is no longer able to furnish samples, and not withdrawing deposit during the required storage period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositors should ensure they can meet replacement obligations and understand withdrawal restrictions under contract terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collection's Right to Refuse Deposits
rubrics_metrics.description: Collections reserve the right to refuse acceptance of material that presents unacceptable risk or is technically unsuitable to handle (explicitly stated for ECACC and other collections).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Risk assessments and prior communication can reduce refusal risk; collections may require pre-submission review (e.g., ECACC risk assessment) and will advise on suitability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Acceptance Criteria for Plasmids and Recombinants
rubrics_metrics.description: NCIMB and ECACC specific criteria for accepting plasmids: plasmids cloned in a host must have host hazard category no higher than ACDP Group 2; naked plasmid DNA must be deposited frozen in appropriate solution and plasmid phenotypic markers must be expressible/detectable; plasmids must be stable on freezing/freeze-drying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositors of plasmids should ensure host hazard classification, stability under preservation, and detectable markers; follow collection-recommended buffers (e.g., EDTA) for naked DNA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seed Acceptance Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: NCIMB accepts orthodox seeds (can be dried and stored at -20°C or lower) but not recalcitrant seeds (e.g., cocoa, rubber). Acceptance and furnishing of seeds are subject to Plant Health Order compliance and prior notification is recommended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositors should notify NCIMB in advance to ensure regulatory compliance; unnotified seed shipments may be delayed or returned by customs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of Guidance and Notes for Depositors
rubrics_metrics.description: Collections provide varying levels of guidance: some make detailed notes available (IMI makes detailed notes; ECACC guidance provided on application form), others do not yet have guidance notes (CCAP, NCYC) or provide limited historical references (NCTC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prospective depositors should consult the collection's guidance materials or contact the collection for clarification prior to deposit.
